name: Shield Block
subtitle: Feat 1 · general

blocks.v: While you have your raise a shield, you would take damage from a physical attack.

blocks.t: You snap your shield in place to ward off a blow. Your shield prevents you from taking an amount of damage up to the shield's Hardness. You and the shield each take any remaining damage, possibly breaking or destroying the shield.

name: Toughness
subtitle: Feat 1 · general

blocks.t: You can withstand more punishment than most before succumbing. Increase your maximum Hit Points by your level. The DC of recovery checks is equal to 9 + your dying condition value (page 459).

name: Fleet
subtitle: Feat 1 · general

blocks.t: You move more quickly on foot. Your Speed increases by 5 feet.

name: Diehard
subtitle: Feat 1 · general

blocks.t: It takes more to kill you than most. You die from the dying condition at dying 5, rather than dying 4.

name: Sudden Charge
subtitle: Feat 1 · barbarian

blocks.t: With a quick sprint, you dash up to your foe and swing. Stride twice. If you end your movement within melee reach of at least one enemy, you can make a melee Strike against that enemy. You can use Sudden Charge while Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.

name: Power Attack
subtitle: Feat 1 · fighter

blocks.t: You unleash a particularly powerful attack that clobbers your foe but leaves you a bit unsteady. Make a melee Strike. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. If you're at least 10th level, increase this to two extra dice, and if you're at least 18th level, increase it to three extra dice.

name: Twin Takedown
subtitle: Feat 1 · flourish

blocks.v: You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand.

blocks.t: You swiftly attack your hunt prey with both weapons. Make two Strike against your hunted prey, one with each of the required weapons. If both hit the same hunted prey, combine their damage for the purpose of its resistances and weaknesses. Apply your multiple attack penalty to each Strike normally.

name: Ward Medic
subtitle: Feat 2 · general

blocks.t: You've studied in large medical wards, treating several patients at once and tending to all their needs. When you use Treat Disease or Treat Wounds, you can treat up to two targets. If you're a master in Medicine, you can treat up to four targets, and if you're legendary, you can treat up to eight targets.

name: Second Wind
subtitle: Feat 2 · barbarian

blocks.t: You can enter a second rage, but afterward you need to catch your breath. You can Rage without waiting for 1 minute after the previous Rage (or 1 round, with quick rage), but when you end this second Rage, you're fatigued until you rest for 10 minutes.

subtitle: Feat 2 · barbarian

blocks.t: When you Rage, your sense of smell improves. You gain imprecise scent with a range of 30 feet.

name: Adapted Cantrip
subtitle: Feat 1 · human

blocks.t: Through study of multiple magical traditions, you've altered a spell to suit your spellcasting style. Choose one cantrip from a magical tradition other than your own. If you have a spell repertoire or a spellbook, replace one of the cantrips you know or have in your spellbook with the chosen spell. If you prepare spells without a spellbook (if you're a cleric or druid, for example), one of your cantrips must always be the chosen spell, and you prepare the rest normally. You can cast this cantrip as a spell of your class's tradition.
If you swap or retrain this cantrip later, you can choose its replacement from the same alternate tradition or a different one.

name: Assurance
subtitle: Feat 1 · fortune

blocks.v: trained in at least one skill

blocks.t: Even in the worst circumstances, you can perform basic tasks. Choose a skill you're trained in. You can forgo rolling a skill check for that skill to instead receive a result of 10 + your proficiency bonus (do not apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers).

name: Titan Wrestler
subtitle: Feat 1 · general

blocks.t: You can attempt to Disarm, Grapple, Shove, or Trip creatures up to two sizes larger than you, or up to three sizes larger than you if you're legendary in Athletics.
